description:
## The rule that is wrong

`resolve_closure_call` (jobs/semantic.rs) has two exits that manufacture `any`:

    let Some(clauses) = world.types_mut().callable_value_clauses(&callee_ty) else {
        // A callable value the engine cannot resolve to closure targets is a
        // dynamic edge: `any` is earned here, as at provider boundaries.
        return Ok((None, Some(any_ty(world))));
    };
    ...
    if selected_targets.is_empty() {
        if named_concrete_target { return Ok((None, return_ty)); }
        return Ok((None, Some(any_ty(world))));
    }

Both read "I cannot resolve this callee" as "this callee is dynamic". For a
callee type that still carries TYPE VARIABLES that reading is wrong: a variable
is not-yet-known, not anything-at-all. The function's own doc comment, twelve
lines further down, states the correct principle for the sibling case and is
violated by these two exits:

    // ... which is *absence of evidence*, not proof of a dynamic edge. We must
    // not manufacture `any` from that absence: the cumulative `ReturnType` join
    // would union the stale `any` and never retract it once the target settles
    // to its real type.

## Measured evidence (probe at both exits, HEAD 7a69440b7)

Program (three distinct lambdas at one `Enum.drop_while`; two is green, three
is not):

    fn main() do
      xs = [1, 2, 3]
      dbg(Enum.drop_while(xs, fn (x) -> x < 0 end))
      dbg(Enum.drop_while(xs, fn (x) -> x < 0 end))
      dbg(Enum.drop_while(xs, fn (x) -> x < 0 end))
    end

Both exits fire, both inside `List.reduce_while_cont/3` at its single closure
call `reducer.(head, acc)`:

    any@no-clauses: caller_inputs=([any], any, a2) -> r0
                    callee_ty=a2                    args=[any, any]
    any@no-clauses: caller_inputs=([any], {[a1_0_e], :false}, a2) -> r0
                    callee_ty=a2                    args=[any, {[any], :false}]
    any@no-target:  caller_inputs=([int], any, a2) -> r0
                    callee_ty=(int | a2_p0, a2_p1 | {[], :true}) -> none
                    args=[int, any]
    any@no-target:  caller_inputs=([int], {[a1_0_e], :true}, a2) -> r0
                    callee_ty=(int | a2_p0, a2_p1 | {[], :true}) -> none
                    args=[int, {[], :true}]

Read the callee types:

- `a2` is a BARE SPEC VARIABLE. The reducer slot was never instantiated.
- `(int | a2_p0, a2_p1 | {[], :true}) -> none` is the real closure arrow JOINED
  with the un-instantiated template, parameter by parameter, and its return has
  degenerated to `none` -- an un-instantiated variable in return position.

Neither is a dynamic callee. Both are half-substituted templates, and `any` is
manufactured from them and then never retracted, because the value-type join is
cumulative.

## Why this is the live `enum_take_drop_split` red

The manufactured `any` is exactly the `semantic result type` the
fz-f98.14.11 guard reports:

    error[artifact/incomplete-semantic-plan]: public closure callsite 0 settled
    return `{:cont, {[int], :false}} | {:cont, {[], :true}}` disagrees with its
    semantic result type `any`

The CallSiteSummary resolved the reducer's targets precisely; the value type
says `any` because of these two exits. Two facts about one callsite, derived
from different evidence, disagree -- and the guard makes them say so.

## Experiment already run (do not redo it)

Gating BOTH exits on `world.types().has_vars(&callee_ty)` and returning
absence-of-evidence instead of `any`:

    if world.types().has_vars(&callee_ty) {
        return Ok((None, None));          // no-clauses exit
        return Ok((None, return_ty));     // no-target exit
    }

Result, measured:

- The N-lambda ladder goes fully GREEN. It previously failed at N = 3, 4, 5, 7,
  8, 9 and passed at 2, 6 and >= 10 (deterministic, and the non-monotone shape
  that falsified every budget-threshold explanation). Every N now passes.
- `cargo test --lib`: 1443 passed / 4 failed -- IDENTICAL to HEAD, no new
  failures.
- `fixture_matrix --test-threads=1`: 410 passed / 3 failed -- IDENTICAL to HEAD,
  no new failures.
- `enum_take_drop_split` moves OFF the `any` guard and onto a new, narrower
  failure:

      thread 'main' panicked at src/compiler2/jobs/transport.rs:1280:
      a resume payload value must have an analyzed type

So the six lines are directionally right and regression-free, but they are not
the whole ticket: they expose one downstream consumer that depended on the
manufactured `any`.

## The remaining gap

`resume_payload_ty` (jobs/transport.rs:1273) reads `value_types` and `expect`s
an entry:

    fn resume_payload_ty(facts: &ExecutableFacts, entry: ControlEntryId) -> Ty {
        let value = resume_payload_value(facts, entry);
        facts.analysis().value_types.get(&value).copied()
            .expect("a resume payload value must have an analyzed type")
    }

With the manufactured `any` gone, a resume-payload value on the
`{:suspend, ...}` continuation path has no entry. Decide which is true before
writing code:

1. the value is genuinely un-analyzed this round and transport must WAIT for it
   (the pull-graph answer, consistent with the fz-go4 wait discipline); or
2. the value is unreachable and the resume entry should not have been produced
   at all (the phantom-executable answer, fz-f98.5 mechanism 1); or
3. the resume payload has a settled type available from another fact and this
   consumer is reading the wrong one.

Do not paper over it with `unwrap_or(any)` -- that reinstates the exact defect
this ticket removes, one layer downstream.

## Relation to fz-f98.10

fz-f98.10's LOCUS claim is confirmed: swapping `List.reduce_while` for
`Enum.reduce_while` in an otherwise identical program is the whole delta, so the
protocol callback hop is what produces the variable-typed callee (its spec
`(t(a), b, (a, b) -> {:cont, b} | {:halt, c}) :: b | c` cannot bind `a` from a
bare-opaque `t(a)`, so nothing instantiates the reducer slot). But f98.10's
PRESCRIPTION -- model the protocol domain as a bound its impls satisfy -- is not
what fixes this, and f98.10's own stated Checks already pass at HEAD. This
ticket is the actionable half; f98.10 should be re-scoped to whatever remains
after it.

## Checks

- The N-lambda `Enum.drop_while` ladder is green for every N.
- `enum_take_drop_split` compiles and matches its Elixir oracle on interp, run
  and build.
- No closure callsite reports a `semantic result type` of `any` that its
  CallSiteSummary resolved precisely.
- A lib regression test pins "a callee that still carries variables yields
  absence, not `any`" at `resolve_closure_call`.
- Full lib + matrix at baseline or better.
title: resolve_closure_call earns `any` for a callee that still carries type variables: unknown is treated as dynamic
